claim: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters constitute the largest family of primary active transporters.
source: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters constitute the largest family of primary active transporters, responsible for many physiological processes and human maladies.
evidence: This is a general characterization statement about ABC transporters that draws from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: ABC transporters are responsible for many physiological processes and human maladies.
source: ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters constitute the largest family of primary active transporters, responsible for many physiological processes and human maladies.
evidence: This statement reflects established scientific consensus about the biological importance of ABC transporters.

claim: A single conformational switch by ATP binding drives unidirectional substrate translocation in TmrAB.
source: We reveal that a single conformational switch by ATP binding drives unidirectional substrate translocation.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data from single-turnover analyses.

claim: ATP hydrolysis and phosphate release launch the return to the resting state after the power stroke.
source: After this power stroke, ATP hydrolysis and phosphate release launch the return to the resting state, which facilitates nucleotide exchange and a new round of substrate binding and translocation.
evidence: This finding is supported by experimental data showing temporal correlation between ATP hydrolysis, phosphate release, and conformational return.

claim: ABC transporters shuttle chemically diverse compounds across cell membranes.
source: Ubiquitous in all phyla of life, ABC transporters shuttle chemically diverse compounds across cell membranes, ranging from peptides and proteins to lipids, metabolites, antibiotics, and drugs (Dean et al., 2001; Rees et al., 2009; Thomas and Tampé, 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: ABC transporters are ubiquitous in all phyla of life.
source: Ubiquitous in all phyla of life, ABC transporters shuttle chemically diverse compounds across cell membranes, ranging from peptides and proteins to lipids, metabolites, antibiotics, and drugs (Dean et al., 2001; Rees et al., 2009; Thomas and Tampé, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to established literature.

claim: Substrate transport by ABC transporters is facilitated by large conformational changes chemomechanically coupled to ATP hydrolysis.
source: Substrate transport is facilitated by large conformational changes, which are chemomechanically coupled to the hydrolysis of ATP (Abele and Tampé, 2004; Higgins and Linton, 2004; Senior and Gadsby, 1997).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: ABC exporters are composed of two nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs) and two transmembrane domains (TMDs).
source: ABC exporters are composed of two nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs), responsible for ATP binding and hydrolysis, and two transmembrane domains (TMDs) forming the substrate translocation pathway.
evidence: This is a structural description based on established knowledge of ABC transporter architecture.

claim: NBDs are responsible for ATP binding and hydrolysis in ABC exporters.
source: ABC exporters are composed of two nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs), responsible for ATP binding and hydrolysis, and two transmembrane domains (TMDs) forming the substrate translocation pathway.
evidence: This functional assignment is based on established knowledge of ABC transporter structure-function relationships.

claim: TMDs form the substrate translocation pathway in ABC exporters.
source: ABC exporters are composed of two nucleotide-binding domains (NBDs), responsible for ATP binding and hydrolysis, and two transmembrane domains (TMDs) forming the substrate translocation pathway.
evidence: This functional assignment is based on established knowledge of ABC transporter structure-function relationships.

claim: ABC exporters are involved in cystic fibrosis.
source: ABC exporters are involved in multifold physiological pathways and human diseases, ranging from cystic fibrosis to acquired multidrug resistance in cancer chemotherapy (Csanády et al., 2019; Robey et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on ABC transporter-related diseases.

claim: ABC exporters are involved in acquired multidrug resistance in cancer chemotherapy.
source: ABC exporters are involved in multifold physiological pathways and human diseases, ranging from cystic fibrosis to acquired multidrug resistance in cancer chemotherapy (Csanády et al., 2019; Robey et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on ABC transporter-related diseases.

claim: TAP plays a critical role in the adaptive immune response against intracellular pathogens and tumors.
source: The transporter associated with antigen processing (TAP) plays a critical role in the adaptive immune response against intracellular pathogens and tumors (Blum et al., 2013; Trowitzsch and Tampé, 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to literature on TAP function.

claim: More than half of all human ABC transporters have two functionally asymmetric ATP-binding sites.
source: Notably, more than half of all human ABC transporters have two functionally asymmetric ATP-binding sites (canonical vs. non-canonical).
evidence: This is a statement about the prevalence of asymmetric ATP sites in human ABC transporters, based on established knowledge.

claim: TmrAB represents a structural and functional homolog of the TAP complex.
source: The Thermus thermophilus multidrug resistance transport complex TmrAB represents a structural and functional homolog of the TAP complex with an overlapping peptide specificity and can restore antigen presentation in human TAP-deficient cells (Kim et al., 2015; Nöll et al., 2017; Zutz et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: TmrAB has overlapping peptide specificity with TAP.
source: The Thermus thermophilus multidrug resistance transport complex TmrAB represents a structural and functional homolog of the TAP complex with an overlapping peptide specificity and can restore antigen presentation in human TAP-deficient cells (Kim et al., 2015; Nöll et al., 2017; Zutz et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: TmrAB can restore antigen presentation in human TAP-deficient cells.
source: The Thermus thermophilus multidrug resistance transport complex TmrAB represents a structural and functional homolog of the TAP complex with an overlapping peptide specificity and can restore antigen presentation in human TAP-deficient cells (Kim et al., 2015; Nöll et al., 2017; Zutz et al., 2011).
evidence: This functional capability is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Eight high-resolution cryo-EM structures of TmrAB in different states and conformations were determined.
source: In particular, eight high-resolution cryo-EM structures of TmrAB in different states and conformations were determined, comprising two inward-facing (IF), four outward-facing (OF), and two asymmetric post-hydrolysis states (Hofmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous structural study.

claim: The eight cryo-EM structures of TmrAB comprise two inward-facing (IF), four outward-facing (OF), and two asymmetric post-hydrolysis states.
source: In particular, eight high-resolution cryo-EM structures of TmrAB in different states and conformations were determined, comprising two inward-facing (IF), four outward-facing (OF), and two asymmetric post-hydrolysis states (Hofmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This structural information is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Two major transitions from IF-to-OF and OF-to-IF conformation can be defined in TmrAB.
source: Based on this detailed insight, two major transitions from IF-to-OF and OF-to-IF conformation can be defined.
evidence: This is inferred from the structural data mentioned in the previous sentence.

claim: The functional roles of ATP binding and ATP hydrolysis in the substrate translocation cycle are poorly defined.
source: However, the functional roles of ATP binding and ATP hydrolysis in the substrate translocation cycle are poorly defined.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field prior to this study.

claim: ABC exporters have not been analyzed by single-turnover assays prior to this study.
source: Notably, exporters to our knowledge ABC have not been analyzed by single-turnover assays, which would require full transport activity of all correctly reconstituted ABC transporters in liposomes paired with sensitive detection of the translocated substrate.
evidence: This is a statement about the lack of previous studies using this methodology.

claim: Some ABC exporters have been described as uncoupled molecular machines that undergo multiple rounds of ATP hydrolysis per translocated substrate.
source: Furthermore, some ABC exporters have been described as uncoupled molecular machines that undergo multiple rounds of ATP hydrolysis per translocated substrate (Bock et al., 2019; Eytan et al., 1996; Nöll et al., 2017; Zehnpfennig et al., 2009; Zollmann et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The significance of futile cycles in ABC exporters is largely unclear.
source: The significance of these futile cycles, however, is largely unclear.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: TmrAB was reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs providing an optimal lipid environment for full activity and conformational freedom.
source: The translocation complex TmrAB was reconstituted in lipid nanodiscs or liposomes providing an optimal lipid environment (Bechara et al., 2015) for full activity and conformational freedom (Hofmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on reconstitution methods.

claim: The IF-to-OF transition by ATP binding drives unidirectional substrate translocation across the membrane.
source: We delineate that a single conformational switch from the IF-to-OF conformation, triggered by ATP binding, drives unidirectional substrate translocation across the membrane.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: After ATP hydrolysis and phosphate release from the canonical site, the OF-to-IF transition is launched.
source: After ATP hydrolysis in and phosphate release from the canonical site, the OF-to-IF transition is launched, which allows for nucleotide exchange and a new round of substrate processing.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data.

claim: The OF-to-IF transition allows for nucleotide exchange and a new round of substrate processing.
source: After ATP hydrolysis in and phosphate release from the canonical site, the OF-to-IF transition is launched, which allows for nucleotide exchange and a new round of substrate processing.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of the conformational cycle.

claim: The catalytic glutamate was substituted by glutamine at the canonical ATP site in TmrAEQB to slowdown ATP turnover.
source: In order to kinetically separate the events of ATP binding and hydrolysis, we substituted the catalytic glutamate by glutamine at the canonical ATP site (TmrAE523QB, TmrAEQB) to slowdown the ATP turnover.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental design and mutagenesis performed.

claim: Wildtype TmrAB and TmrAEQB are equivalent in equilibrium peptide- and nucleotide-binding.
source: By scintillation proximity assays (SPA), we confirmed that wildtype TmrAB and TmrAEQB are equivalent in equilibrium peptide- and nucleotide-binding (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Key residues involved in peptide binding are rearranged upon the IF-to-OF transition.
source: When comparing our high-resolution cryo-EM structures of IF and OF conformers (Hofmann et al., 2019), we found that key residues involved in peptide binding are rearranged upon the IF-to-OF transition.
evidence: This is based on structural comparison from cryo-EM data cited from a previous study.

claim: Transmembrane helices TM2, TM3, and TM4 frame the substrate-binding site in the IF conformation.
source: Transmembrane helices TM2, TM3, and TM4, framing the substrate-binding site in the IF conformation, get closely packed together in the OF state to form a tightly sealed intracellular gate (Figure 1a).
evidence: This structural observation is supported by Figure 1a showing the conformational changes.

claim: TM2, TM3, and TM4 get closely packed together in the OF state to form a tightly sealed intracellular gate.
source: Transmembrane helices TM2, TM3, and TM4, framing the substrate-binding site in the IF conformation, get closely packed together in the OF state to form a tightly sealed intracellular gate (Figure 1a).
evidence: This structural observation is supported by Figure 1a.

claim: After the IF-to-OF transition induced by ATP binding, the association of radiolabeled peptides to TmrAEQB was precluded.
source: After the IF-to-OF transition induced by ATP binding, the association of radiolabeled peptides to TmrAEQB was precluded (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b.

claim: The impairment of substrate binding after the IF-to-OF transition was shown by fluorescence anisotropy using the fluorescent C4F peptide.
source: The impairment of substrate binding was also shown by fluorescence anisotropy using the fluorescent C4F peptide (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: Loss of peptide binding correlates with the concentration of ATP added to induce the IF-to-OF transition.
source: Loss of peptide binding correlates with the concentration of ATP added to induce the IF-to-OF transition, which is monitored by fluorescence anisotropy using fluorescent peptides (Figure 1d) and by SPA utilizing radiolabeled peptides (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The EC50 of ATP for inducing loss of peptide binding is 30 µM.
source: The EC50 of 30 µM is consistent with the equilibrium dissociation constant of Mg2+-ATP (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is derived from experimental data shown in Figure 1d and 1e.

claim: The EC50 of 30 µM is consistent with the equilibrium dissociation constant of Mg2+-ATP.
source: The EC50 of 30 µM is consistent with the equilibrium dissociation constant of Mg2+-ATP (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental measurements.

claim: A similar loss of substrate binding was observed after nucleotide trapping in the OF conformation by ATPγS.
source: It is worth mentioning that we observed a similar loss of substrate binding after nucleotide trapping in the OF conformation by ATPγS, a slowly hydrolyzing ATP analog (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Binding of radiolabeled and fluorescent peptides was not affected by Mg2+-ADP.
source: Using the same experimental conditions, binding of radiolabeled and fluorescent peptides was not affected by Mg2+-ADP (Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 2), although Mg2+-ADP and Mg2+-ATP display similar affinities for TmrAB in the IF conformation (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1d, Figure 1e, and Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mg2+-ADP and Mg2+-ATP display similar affinities for TmrAB in the IF conformation.
source: Using the same experimental conditions, binding of radiolabeled and fluorescent peptides was not affected by Mg2+-ADP (Figure 1d and Figure 1—figure supplement 2), although Mg2+-ADP and Mg2+-ATP display similar affinities for TmrAB in the IF conformation (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Only ATP and not ADP can drive the IF-to-OF transition.
source: In conclusion, only ATP and not ADP can drive the IF-to-OF transition, which in turn abrogates high-affinity substrate binding to the ABC transporter.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the experimental data showing differential effects of ATP and ADP on peptide binding.

claim: The IF-to-OF transition abrogates high-affinity substrate binding to the ABC transporter.
source: In conclusion, only ATP and not ADP can drive the IF-to-OF transition, which in turn abrogates high-affinity substrate binding to the ABC transporter.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing loss of peptide binding after ATP-induced conformational switch.

claim: The half-life of the nucleotide-occluded state at 20 °C was 24 min.
source: The half-life of the nucleotide-occluded state at 20 °C was 24 min, which is in accordance with the ATP turnover of 29 ± 1 min at room temperature (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c and 2d.

claim: The ATP turnover at room temperature is 29 ± 1 min.
source: The half-life of the nucleotide-occluded state at 20 °C was 24 min, which is in accordance with the ATP turnover of 29 ± 1 min at room temperature (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The half-life of the nucleotide-occluded state was slightly affected by temperature.
source: The half-life of the nucleotide-occluded state was slightly affected by temperature. At 4 °C, the half-life was prolonged to 34 min and reduced to 19 min at 45 °C (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: At 4 °C, the half-life of the nucleotide-occluded state was prolonged to 34 min.
source: At 4 °C, the half-life was prolonged to 34 min and reduced to 19 min at 45 °C (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: At 45 °C, the half-life of the nucleotide-occluded state was reduced to 19 min.
source: At 4 °C, the half-life was prolonged to 34 min and reduced to 19 min at 45 °C (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Only 50% of bound nucleotides were released at 4 °C suggesting an asymmetric opening of both ATP sites.
source: Interestingly, only 50% of bound nucleotides were released at 4 °C suggesting an asymmetric opening of both ATP sites (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1, with interpretation suggesting asymmetry.

claim: IF TmrAEQB displayed fast peptide binding in the absence of Mg-ATP.
source: In the absence of Mg-ATP, IF TmrAEQB displayed fast peptide binding, which was linearly increasing over time, typical of SPA-based peptide-binding assays (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: A mono-exponential recovery of peptide binding with a half-life of 24 min was observed during the OF-to-IF return.
source: However, we observed a mono-exponential recovery of peptide binding with a half-life of 24 min, reaching the level determined before nucleotide trapping after 60 min (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: Peptide binding reached the level determined before nucleotide trapping after 60 min.
source: However, we observed a mono-exponential recovery of peptide binding with a half-life of 24 min, reaching the level determined before nucleotide trapping after 60 min (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The conformational cycle is fully reversible.
source: This demonstrates the full reversibility of the conformational cycle, which we can dissect into two single-turnover events.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that peptide binding fully recovers to pre-trapping levels.

claim: Only one of the two occluded ATP molecules is hydrolyzed within the single OF-to-IF transition.
source: Strikingly, only one of the two occluded ATP molecules is hydrolyzed within the single OF-to-IF transition, approaching a final ATP-to-ADP ratio of 1:1 (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: The final ATP-to-ADP ratio after the OF-to-IF transition approaches 1:1.
source: Strikingly, only one of the two occluded ATP molecules is hydrolyzed within the single OF-to-IF transition, approaching a final ATP-to-ADP ratio of 1:1 (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2f.

claim: The non-equivalence of the two ATP sites in ATP turnover is illustrated by two asymmetric unlocked-return states captured by cryo-EM.
source: This illustrates the non-equivalence of the two ATP sites in ATP turnover as shown by the two asymmetric unlocked-return states captured by cryo-EM (Hofmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous cryo-EM structural data.

claim: The rate of phosphate release complies with the overall ATP hydrolysis rate.
source: The rate of phosphate release complies with the overall ATP hydrolysis rate as well as the rates of nucleotide release and peptide re-binding.
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental rates measured in the study.

claim: The rate of phosphate release complies with the rates of nucleotide release and peptide re-binding.
source: The rate of phosphate release complies with the overall ATP hydrolysis rate as well as the rates of nucleotide release and peptide re-binding.
evidence: This is based on comparison of experimental rates measured in the study.

claim: A single ATP turnover and phosphate release at the consensus site launch the OF-to-IF return.
source: Taken together, a single ATP turnover and phosphate release at the consensus site launch the OF-to-IF return, restoring the peptide-binding site and allowing nucleotide exchange.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing temporal correlation of these events.

claim: The OF-to-IF return restores the peptide-binding site.
source: Taken together, a single ATP turnover and phosphate release at the consensus site launch the OF-to-IF return, restoring the peptide-binding site and allowing nucleotide exchange.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing recovery of peptide binding.

claim: The OF-to-IF return allows nucleotide exchange.
source: Taken together, a single ATP turnover and phosphate release at the consensus site launch the OF-to-IF return, restoring the peptide-binding site and allowing nucleotide exchange.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of the conformational cycle.

claim: TmrAB was reconstituted in liposomes at a lipid-to-protein ratio of 20:1 (w/w).
source: To test whether ATP binding leads to a productive translocation event in the IF-to-OF transition, we reconstituted TmrAEQB in liposomes at a lipid-to-protein ratio of 20:1 (w/w) and performed a single-turnover assay with 50 µM C4F peptide (Figure 3a), which is well above its KD value of 6.8 µM (Nöll et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental setup.

claim: The KD value of C4F peptide is 6.8 µM.
source: To test whether ATP binding leads to a productive translocation event in the IF-to-OF transition, we reconstituted TmrAEQB in liposomes at a lipid-to-protein ratio of 20:1 (w/w) and performed a single-turnover assay with 50 µM C4F peptide (Figure 3a), which is well above its KD value of 6.8 µM (Nöll et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: TmrAEQB with occluded Mg2+-ATP remains arrested in the OF conformation with a half-life of 24 min.
source: Given that TmrAEQB with occluded Mg2+-ATP remains arrested in the OF conformation with a half-life of 24 min, these data indicate that ATP binding with the ensuring IF-to-OF switch – and not ATP hydrolysis – represent the power stroke driving substrate translocation (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is based on previous experimental data showing the half-life of the nucleotide-occluded state.

claim: ATP binding with the ensuring IF-to-OF switch represents the power stroke driving substrate translocation.
source: Given that TmrAEQB with occluded Mg2+-ATP remains arrested in the OF conformation with a half-life of 24 min, these data indicate that ATP binding with the ensuring IF-to-OF switch – and not ATP hydrolysis – represent the power stroke driving substrate translocation (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a key conclusion based on experimental data from single-turnover assays.

claim: ATP hydrolysis does not represent the power stroke driving substrate translocation.
source: Given that TmrAEQB with occluded Mg2+-ATP remains arrested in the OF conformation with a half-life of 24 min, these data indicate that ATP binding with the ensuring IF-to-OF switch – and not ATP hydrolysis – represent the power stroke driving substrate translocation (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a key conclusion based on experimental data from single-turnover assays.

claim: For proteoliposomes incubated with Mg2+-ATP, a substantially higher peptide level was observed compared to Mg2+-ADP after flotation in sucrose density gradients.
source: For proteoliposomes incubated with Mg2+-ATP, we observed a substantially higher peptide level compared to Mg2+-ADP.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from flotation assays shown in Figure 3c.

claim: The level of translocated C4F peptides correlated with the amount of TmrAEQB in the floated liposome fraction.
source: Notably, the level of translocated C4F peptides correlated with the amount of TmrAEQB in the floated liposome fraction.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from flotation assays.

claim: Fractions lacking TmrAB showed only background fluorescence similar to proteoliposomes incubated with ADP.
source: In contrast, fractions lacking TmrAB showed only background fluorescence similar to proteoliposomes incubated with ADP, for which the peptide level was independent of the amount of reconstituted TmrAEQB in the corresponding fraction.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from flotation assays.

claim: 50% of TmrAEQB complexes have right-side-out orientation in liposomes.
source: As monitored via anti-His immunoblotting, 50% of the His-tags were cleaved, reflecting TmrAB complex with the right-side-out orientation while equal loading of proteoliposomes was controlled by instant blue staining (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from TEV protease cleavage assays shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: 95% of TmrAEQB complexes were effectively reconstituted in proteoliposomes.
source: Secondly, the reconstitution efficiency was determined by carbonate crush and flotation in sucrose density gradients. Hereby, 95% of TmrAEQB complexes were effectively reconstituted in proteoliposomes and were detected in the top fractions as quantified by anti-His immunoblotting (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The average proteoliposome diameter is ~160 nm.
source: Thirdly, the average proteoliposomes diameter (~160 nm) was measured by single-particle tracking (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Each liposome contains ~30 correctly-oriented, energizable transport complexes.
source: Finally, we calculated for each liposome ~30 correctly-oriented, energizable transport complexes.
evidence: This is calculated based on the experimental characterization of proteoliposomes.

claim: A nearly stoichiometric coupling of ~0.5 translocated peptides per TmrAEQB complex was calculated.
source: Notably, based on the number of translocated peptides per liposome, a nearly stoichiometric coupling of ~0.5 translocated peptides per TmrAEQB complex was calculated.
evidence: This is calculated based on experimental data from transport assays.

claim: A 100-fold increase in transported peptides was observed with ATP compared to ADP in wildtype TmrAB.
source: After incubation with ATP for 5 min at 45 °C, a 100-fold increase in transported peptides was observed as compared to the background control with ADP (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Substrate transport was observed for 98% of TmrAB-positive liposomes.
source: It is important mentioning that substrate transport was observed for 98% of TmrAB-positive liposomes.
evidence: This is based on flow cytometry analysis of single liposomes.

claim: A linear increase of the mean fluorescence intensity over the range of 1 to 100 peptides per liposome was observed in calibration experiments.
source: We observed a linear increase of the mean fluorescence intensity over the range of 1 to 100 peptides per liposome (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by calibration data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Proteoliposomes incubated with ATP showed a substantial increase in fluorescent peptide compared to the background level with ADP under single-turnover conditions.
source: Proteoliposomes incubated with ATP showed a substantial increase in fluorescent peptide compared to the background level with ADP (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Peptide translocation by TmrAEQB showed a biphasic time dependency characterized by a fast burst phase and a much slower linear steady-state rate.
source: Peptide translocation by TmrAEQB showed a biphasic time dependency characterized by a fast burst phase (pre-steady state) and a much slower linear steady-state rate (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c.

claim: Within the first minutes, the transported peptides increased until all TmrAEQB complexes had been switched and arrested in the pre-hydrolytic state.
source: Within the first minutes, the transported peptides increased until all TmrAEQB complexes had been switched and arrested in the pre-hydrolytic state (burst phase).
evidence: This is based on interpretation of the biphasic kinetics observed in Figure 5c.

claim: In the burst phase (0–5 min), ~30 peptides are transported per liposome.
source: In the burst phase (0–5 min), however,~30 peptides are transported per liposome (y-axis intercept of the linear term), reflecting the number of transport-competent TmrAEQB complexes per liposome (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5c and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: The number of transported peptides in the burst phase reflects the number of transport-competent TmrAEQB complexes per liposome.
source: In the burst phase (0–5 min), however,~30 peptides are transported per liposome (y-axis intercept of the linear term), reflecting the number of transport-competent TmrAEQB complexes per liposome (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between the burst phase amplitude and the number of correctly oriented transporters.

claim: Proteoliposomes displayed an additive accumulation of peptides along each IF-to-OF switch in sequential cycles.
source: Proteoliposomes displayed an additive accumulation of peptides along each IF-to-OF switch, while the number of translocated peptides per liposome did not change during each OF-to-IF return, indicating that peptides are not retro-translocated during the OF-to-IF transition (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: The number of translocated peptides per liposome did not change during each OF-to-IF return.
source: Proteoliposomes displayed an additive accumulation of peptides along each IF-to-OF switch, while the number of translocated peptides per liposome did not change during each OF-to-IF return, indicating that peptides are not retro-translocated during the OF-to-IF transition (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Peptides are not retro-translocated during the OF-to-IF transition.
source: Proteoliposomes displayed an additive accumulation of peptides along each IF-to-OF switch, while the number of translocated peptides per liposome did not change during each OF-to-IF return, indicating that peptides are not retro-translocated during the OF-to-IF transition (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that peptide levels remain constant during the return phase.

claim: ~1.3 peptides are translocated per correctly oriented TmrAEQB upon each IF-to-OF transition.
source: We calculated that ~1.3 peptides are translocated per correctly oriented TmrAEQB upon each IF-to-OF transition.
evidence: This is calculated based on experimental data from sequential transport cycles.

claim: During the second IF-to-OF switch, the fluorescence signal of C4AF647 remained constant in dual-substrate translocation experiments.
source: Notably, during the second IF-to-OF switch, the fluorescence signal of C4AF647 remained constant, demonstrating that substrate transport occurs unidirectionally.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from dual-substrate translocation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Substrate transport occurs unidirectionally.
source: Notably, during the second IF-to-OF switch, the fluorescence signal of C4AF647 remained constant, demonstrating that substrate transport occurs unidirectionally.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that previously transported peptides are not released during subsequent cycles.

claim: Sequential rounds of ATP binding drive a unidirectional and stoichiometrically coupled substrate translocation via a single IF-to-OF switch.
source: Taken together, sequential rounds of ATP binding drive a unidirectional and stoichiometrically coupled substrate translocation via a single IF-to-OF switch.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from sequential transport cycles.

claim: ATP hydrolysis and phosphate release in the canonical site is used to master the directionality of the ABC transporter.
source: In turn, ATP hydrolysis and phosphate release in the canonical site is used to master the directionality of the ABC transporter.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations showing that ATP hydrolysis drives the return phase but not substrate translocation.

claim: ATP binding initiates the IF-to-OF transition and is stoichiometrically coupled to substrate translocation.
source: In this work, we advance the quantitative mechanistic understanding of ABC exporters. We reveal that ATP binding, which initiates the IF-to-OF transition, is stoichiometrically coupled to substrate translocation (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Along the power stroke by occlusion of two ATP molecules, the substrate-binding site is remodeled, priming substrate release on the extracellular site.
source: Along this power stroke by occlusion of two ATP molecules, the substrate-binding site is remodeled, priming substrate release on the extracellular site.
evidence: This is inferred from structural and functional data showing loss of substrate binding in the OF state.

claim: ATP hydrolysis and subsequent phosphate release at the consensus site trigger the OF-to-IF return.
source: In contrast, ATP hydrolysis and subsequent phosphate release at the consensus site trigger the OF-to-IF return, which restores substrate binding and nucleotide exchange to start a new translocation cycle.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion supported by experimental data.

claim: The OF-to-IF return restores substrate binding and nucleotide exchange to start a new translocation cycle.
source: In contrast, ATP hydrolysis and subsequent phosphate release at the consensus site trigger the OF-to-IF return, which restores substrate binding and nucleotide exchange to start a new translocation cycle.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing recovery of peptide binding after the return phase.

claim: The IF-to-OF transition initiated by ATP binding abolishes peptide binding.
source: By using equilibrium ligand-binding assays, we demonstrate that the IF-to-OF transition initiated by ATP binding abolishes peptide binding.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from equilibrium binding assays.

claim: The use of a catalytically less active variant in combination with Mg-ATP is an effective strategy for colonizing ABC exporters in the pre-hydrolytic OF state.
source: The use of a catalytically less active variant in combination with Mg-ATP has been described as an effective strategy for colonizing ABC exporters in the pre-hydrolytic OF state (Hofmann et al., 2019; Kim and Chen, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: A comparison of IF and OF TmrAB points to a drastic reorganization of residues aligning the substrate-binding site.
source: A comparison of IF and OF TmrAB points to a drastic reorganization of residues aligning the substrate-binding site (Hofmann et al., 2019), similar to P-glycoprotein (Martin et al., 2000; Martin et al., 2001), ABCG2 (McDevitt et al., 2008), and MRP1 (Payen et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies of TmrAB and other ABC transporters.

claim: The OF-to-IF return directly correlates with the ATP turnover.
source: In addition, we delineate that the OF-to-IF return directly correlates with (i) the ATP turnover, (ii) the release of inorganic phosphate, (iii) the restoration of peptide binding, and (iv) nucleotide exchange.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing temporal correlation of these events.

claim: The OF-to-IF return directly correlates with the release of inorganic phosphate.
source: In addition, we delineate that the OF-to-IF return directly correlates with (i) the ATP turnover, (ii) the release of inorganic phosphate, (iii) the restoration of peptide binding, and (iv) nucleotide exchange.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing temporal correlation of these events.

claim: The OF-to-IF return directly correlates with the restoration of peptide binding.
source: In addition, we delineate that the OF-to-IF return directly correlates with (i) the ATP turnover, (ii) the release of inorganic phosphate, (iii) the restoration of peptide binding, and (iv) nucleotide exchange.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing temporal correlation of these events.

claim: The OF-to-IF return directly correlates with nucleotide exchange.
source: In addition, we delineate that the OF-to-IF return directly correlates with (i) the ATP turnover, (ii) the release of inorganic phosphate, (iii) the restoration of peptide binding, and (iv) nucleotide exchange.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations of the conformational cycle.

claim: A full recovery of peptide binding was observed, demonstrating reversibility of conformational transitions.
source: We observed a full recovery of peptide binding, demonstrating reversibility of conformational transitions to start subsequent processing cycles.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing complete recovery of peptide binding.

claim: The processive-clamp/ATP-switch model has gained increasing acceptance in the light of new structures of ABC transporters solved in the nucleotide-bound state.
source: The processive-clamp/ATP-switch model (Abele and Tampé, 2004; Higgins and Linton, 2004; Janas et al., 2003) has gained increasing acceptance in the light of new structures of ABC transporters solved in the nucleotide-bound state (Johnson and Chen, 2018; Manolaridis et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to literature on ABC transporter models and structures.

claim: ATP binding drives the single-translocation event of different substrates along the IF-to-OF transition.
source: We uncovered that ATP binding drives the single-translocation event of different substrates along the IF-to-OF transition.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion supported by experimental data from single-turnover assays.

claim: Substrate transport by TmrAEQB is unidirectional.
source: By analyzing sequential steps in the translocation cycle, we revealed that substrate transport by TmrAEQB is unidirectional, which was previously shown for human TAP (Grossmann et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from sequential transport cycles and citation to a previous study on TAP.

claim: Substrate transport by human TAP is unidirectional.
source: By analyzing sequential steps in the translocation cycle, we revealed that substrate transport by TmrAEQB is unidirectional, which was previously shown for human TAP (Grossmann et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: The coupling between ATP hydrolysis and the transported substrate can be quite ineffective, reaching up to 100 ATP-turnover events per translocated substrate.
source: The coupling between ATP hydrolysis and the transported substrate can be quite ineffective, reaching up to 100 ATP-turnover events per translocated substrate (Bock et al., 2019; Manolaridis et al., 2018; Nöll et al., 2017; Zehnpfennig et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Experimental parameters such as detergents, lipid environment, sample preparation, protein activity, and sensitivity of applied methods can substantially affect the energetic coupling.
source: Experimental parameters such as detergents, lipid environment, sample preparation, protein activity, and sensitivity of applied methods can substantially affect the energetic coupling.
evidence: This is a general statement based on knowledge of experimental factors affecting ABC transporter studies.

claim: A coupling ratio of 0.5 to 1.3 peptides per TmrAEQB was revealed by single-turnover approaches.
source: Here, our newly established single-turnover approaches reveal a coupling ratio of 0.5 to 1.3 peptides per TmrAEQB.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from single-turnover assays.

claim: A stoichiometric coupling between a single conformational transition and a translocation event was revealed.
source: Taking the experimental error and sensitivity of these approaches into account, we revealed a stoichiometric coupling between a single conformational transition and a translocation event.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on experimental data from single-turnover assays.

claim: Single-liposome approaches revealed a fast burst phase followed by a slower steady-state phase.
source: Our new single-liposome approaches revealed a fast burst phase followed by a slower steady-state phase, indicating that a step after substrate translocation is rate-limiting.
evidence: This is based on experimental data from time-dependent transport assays.

claim: A step after substrate translocation is rate-limiting.
source: Our new single-liposome approaches revealed a fast burst phase followed by a slower steady-state phase, indicating that a step after substrate translocation is rate-limiting.
evidence: This is inferred from the biphasic kinetics observed in transport assays.

claim: Two asymmetric ADP/ATP-bound states were captured under steady-state conditions in cryo-EM structures of TmrAB.
source: In our cryo-EM structures of TmrAB, we captured two asymmetric ADP/ATP-bound states under steady-state conditions, leading to the assumption that the separation of the NBD dimer represents the rate-limiting step (Hofmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous cryo-EM study.

claim: The separation of the NBD dimer represents the rate-limiting step.
source: In our cryo-EM structures of TmrAB, we captured two asymmetric ADP/ATP-bound states under steady-state conditions, leading to the assumption that the separation of the NBD dimer represents the rate-limiting step (Hofmann et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on structural data.

claim: The rates of phosphate, ATP, and ADP release correlate with the OF-to-IF transition.
source: Here, we demonstrate that the rates of phosphate, ATP, and ADP release correlate with the OF-to-IF transition.
evidence: This is based on experimental data showing temporal correlation of these events.

claim: The IF-to-OF transition by ATP binding drives unidirectional substrate translocation across the membrane.
source: We uncovered that the IF-to-OF transition by ATP binding drives unidirectional substrate translocation across the membrane.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study supported by experimental data.

claim: Single-turnover approaches will be an indispensable method to unfold hidden facets of conformational coupling, energy transduction, and mechanistic details of substrate translocation by ABC transporters.
source: In the future, single-turnover approaches will be an indispensable method to unfold hidden facets of conformational coupling, energy transduction, and mechanistic details of substrate translocation by ABC transporters but also other membrane translocation machineries.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the future utility of the methodology.
